1.why: verify-token only accepts the token whose SHA-256 digest matches session.recovery for that same session and marks it used.

2.why: The reset token is stored only on the issuing session; another session has no matching recovery record so the same code cannot verify.

3.why: Password change only sets session.passwordHash on the current recovery session and never invalidates or removes other entries in the sessions map.

4.why: Bun.serve is configured with TLS cert/key and non-HTTPS is rejected, but no minimum TLS version is pinned in code.

5.why: Reset tokens are stored as SHA-256 digests and passwords via bcrypt, but MFA is plaintext in session memory and nothing is truly encrypted at rest.

6.why: No real email is sent; API messages are generic and never echo the contact, though the test token is returned in JSON for the demo.

7.why: Inputs are type-checked, contact is never reflected/stored, HTML uses escapeHtml, and the client inserts text only via textContent.

8.why: Client navigation uses only same-page location.hash routes; no server-side redirect to user-controlled URLs exists.

9.why: There are no email templates or outbound mail; user input is never embedded in HTML email content.

10.why: testResetToken and testMfaCode are returned in API JSON and written to the visible #logs panel and console.

11.why: Passwords are bcrypt-hashed in memory, but the MFA secret is the hardcoded string "482913" in source and session.mfaCode is stored in plaintext.

12.why: There is no password login with defaults, yet every recovery uses the fixed evaluation MFA code 482913, i.e. a built-in default secret.

13.why: Both per-session throttled() and trusted-IP ipThrottled() limit recovery, token, password, and MFA attempts and return 429.

14.why: request always returns the same generic success message regardless of contact and never indicates whether an account exists.

15.why: Reset tokens are randomBytes(32) base64url values, digested and bound to that session’s recovery record with TTL and single-use.
